panels.title: 0 — What this run left behind
panels.description: Which sources hold anything for this id. Read every zero below as 'no record', not as 'broken'. Measured 2026-08-13: 538 distinct run ids exist across test_runs, workflow_metrics and execution_records, and only 158 of them also have rows in llm_traces — 380 have none, so a run that resolves in every panel on this dashboard is the exception rather than the rule. llm_model_calls counts rows that carry a model, not traced rows: of 2,829 model-call rows in llm_traces only 441 carry a workflow_id, because every span CrewAI emits is unattributed and only the backend's own test-generation-workflow span and LLM calls carrying call metadata bind to a run at all. Panel 6 below lists every traced row for this id, including that workflow span, which appears there with blank model columns. browser-use spend never reaches llm_traces at all — it is recoverable only from workflow_metrics, in panel 2. learning_metrics has no panel of its own here; it is counted so that 'learning recorded nothing for this run' is visible rather than merely absent.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM test_runs WHERE run_id = ${run_id:sqlstring}) AS test_runs_rows, (SELECT count(*) FROM workflow_metrics WHERE workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring}) AS workflow_metrics_rows, (SELECT count(*) FROM execution_records WHERE workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring}) AS execution_records_rows, (SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE nullif(model, '') IS NOT NULL) FROM llm_traces WHERE workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring}) AS llm_model_calls, (SELECT count(*) FROM learning_metrics WHERE workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring}) AS learning_metrics_rows

panels.title: 1 — What was asked, and how it ended
panels.description: test_runs is the only record of a run that failed before the gate. A row still at 'running' long after created_at died without reaching either terminal path.

targets.rawSql: SELECT run_id, status, user_query, error_message, created_at, updated_at, now() - created_at AS age FROM test_runs WHERE run_id = ${run_id:sqlstring}

panels.title: 2 — Gate outcome and cost
panels.description: No row here means the run never reached the metrics block, which runs after the dryrun gate. Go back to panel 1 for the reason. run_wall_s is workflow_duration_s — the whole generation run, not the browser-use element stage timed in panel 5. dryrun_status and crew_stage_metrics carry the key on 33/434 rows, but only 13/434 hold a usable (non-null) value, as of 2026-08-10 — the rest carry a JSON null.

targets.rawSql: SELECT workflow_id, data->>'model_provider' AS provider, data->>'model_name' AS model, (data->>'workflow_duration_s')::numeric AS run_wall_s, (data->>'total_cost')::numeric AS cost_usd, (data->>'crewai_cost')::numeric AS crewai_cost, (data->>'browser_use_cost')::numeric AS browser_use_cost, data->>'dryrun_status' AS gate, (data->>'dryrun_attempts')::int AS attempts, (data->>'dryrun_repairs')::int AS repairs, data->'guardrail_attempts' AS guardrails, (data->>'optimization_fallback_used')::boolean AS learning_fallback FROM workflow_metrics WHERE workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring}

panels.title: 3 — Cost and duration per crew stage
panels.description: planner, assembler, and repair when the gate re-prompted. The deterministic element stage sits between the two kickoffs and is deliberately billed to neither — its time is in panel 5. crew_stage_metrics carries the key on 33/434 rows; only 13/434 hold a usable object as of 2026-08-10 — the rest carry a JSON null, which this panel excludes via jsonb_typeof so it returns no rows instead of erroring.

targets.rawSql: SELECT stage.key AS stage, (stage.value->>'duration_s')::numeric AS duration_s, (stage.value->>'llm_calls')::int AS llm_calls, (stage.value->>'prompt_tokens')::int AS prompt_tokens, (stage.value->>'completion_tokens')::int AS completion_tokens, (stage.value->>'cost')::numeric AS cost_usd FROM workflow_metrics m, jsonb_each(m.data->'crew_stage_metrics') AS stage WHERE m.workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring} AND jsonb_typeof(m.data->'crew_stage_metrics') = 'object' ORDER BY stage.key

panels.title: 4 — Every element, and how its locator was found
panels.description: The key is present on 434/434 metrics rows; one of them holds a JSON null rather than an array, as of 2026-08-10 — this panel excludes it via jsonb_typeof so it returns no rows instead of erroring. fallback_depth above 0 means the primary strategy did not resolve.

targets.rawSql: SELECT e.value->>'element_id' AS element, e.value->>'element_tag' AS tag, e.value->>'locator_approach' AS approach, (e.value->>'fallback_depth')::int AS fallback_depth, (e.value->>'success')::boolean AS success, (e.value->>'is_in_iframe')::boolean AS in_iframe, (e.value->>'is_collection')::boolean AS is_collection, (e.value->>'has_id')::boolean AS has_id, (e.value->>'has_text_content')::boolean AS has_text, (e.value->>'element_data_available')::boolean AS element_data, e.value->>'url_domain' AS domain FROM workflow_metrics m, jsonb_array_elements(m.data->'element_approach_metrics') AS e WHERE m.workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring} AND jsonb_typeof(m.data->'element_approach_metrics') = 'array'

panels.title: 5 — Where the time went
panels.description: poll_overhead_s is how long the backend kept polling after the browser agent had finished. queue_s is the browser-service capacity signal. phase_timings carries the key on 219/434 rows; only 50/434 (11.5%) hold a usable object as of 2026-08-10. The panel's WHERE clause (data ? 'phase_timings') admits the other 169 JSON-null rows too — they are not hidden, they render every column in this panel blank.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (data->'phase_timings'->>'queue_s')::numeric AS queue_s, (data->'phase_timings'->>'session_setup_s')::numeric AS session_setup_s, (data->'phase_timings'->>'agent_run_s')::numeric AS agent_run_s, (data->'phase_timings'->>'poll_wait_s')::numeric AS poll_wait_s, (data->'phase_timings'->>'poll_wait_s')::numeric - (data->'phase_timings'->>'agent_run_s')::numeric AS poll_overhead_s, (data->'agent_diagnostics'->>'llm_429_count')::int AS llm_429s, (data->'agent_diagnostics'->>'retry_lost_s')::numeric AS retry_lost_s, (data->'agent_diagnostics'->>'dom_elements_max')::int AS dom_elements_max, (data->'agent_diagnostics'->>'llm_coverage_gap')::int AS llm_coverage_gap FROM workflow_metrics WHERE workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring} AND data ? 'phase_timings'

panels.title: 6 — Every model call, with prompt and response
panels.description: These rows exist even when the run failed, because they are written per successful LLM call as the run proceeds. This is the only place to recover a failed run's spend. This panel's SQL does not filter on model, so a run's root test-generation-workflow span appears in this list alongside its real model calls, as a row with blank model/prompt/response columns. Attribution, measured against model-call rows rather than the whole table (which is ~97% OpenTelemetry spans): of 2,829 llm_traces rows that carry a model, 441 carry a workflow_id, as of 2026-08-13.

targets.rawSql: SELECT created_at, name, model, duration_ms, status, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd, prompt_text, response_text FROM llm_traces WHERE workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring} ORDER BY start_time_ns

panels.title: 7 — Did the generated test actually pass
panels.description: Empty for a run that was generated but never executed. Only 14 of 123 execution records had a matching metrics row as of 2026-08-10, so an empty panel here is common and is not itself a fault.

targets.rawSql: SELECT test_status, failure_category, failed_keyword, execution_exit_code, execution_duration_ms, domain, code_structure, error_message FROM execution_records WHERE workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring}

panels.title: 8 — The generated Robot code
panels.description: The .robot file this run produced, and the user's correction where one exists. Two sources, deliberately both shown. execution_records.robot_code is populated on 123 of 123 rows (average 1,202 characters) and test_runs.robot_code on 37 of 45, as of 2026-08-13; the two tables share 14 run ids and on all 14 the values were byte-identical. Nothing in the write path guarantees that, so a difference between the two rows is a finding, not a duplicate — preferring one source with coalesce would have hidden it. user_corrected_code is working_code, present on 8 rows, and it is what the user supplied after rejecting the generated test. A row with a blank code column means that table holds a record of the run but no code for it; no row at all means that table has no record of the run — panel 0 at the top says which. Click a cell and choose Inspect value to read or copy the whole file.

targets.rawSql: SELECT 'execution_records' AS source, robot_code, working_code AS user_corrected_code FROM execution_records WHERE workflow_id = ${run_id:sqlstring} UNION ALL SELECT 'test_runs' AS source, robot_code, NULL AS user_corrected_code FROM test_runs WHERE run_id = ${run_id:sqlstring}

panels.title: 9 — Log lines from every service in the run
panels.description: One filter spans the backend, the browser service and the executor, because all three bind the same workflow_id. The executor joined on 2026-08-18; the line counts quoted below were measured before that and cover the first two only. Lines are reformatted for reading — level, logger and the event text — but only where the line is structlog JSON. Lines the JSON parser cannot read pass through byte for byte via the template's {{ __line__ }} fallback. That fallback is load-bearing: measured over 7 days on 2026-08-13, | json returns all 36,289 lines of the combined stream but 25,784 of them fail to parse, because third-party libraries write ANSI-coloured plain text; without the fallback the template renders every one of those as the empty separator '  :: '. The Log level variable defaults to 'every line' for the same reason — its value is .* rather than .+, since a label filter cannot match a level field that is absent and .+ would drop the same 25,784 lines (36,289 down to 10,452). Both narrowing options are therefore structured-only, and their labels say so. A sample run's 280 lines are all JSON-parsable, so neither effect is visible on a single healthy run — which is why a test pins both. Scoped to a single run id by design: bench runs delete their SQL rows but their log lines still reach Loki, so an aggregate log panel would be polluted. LogQL's |= line filter has no fail-closed form: |= "" matches every line (the empty string is a substring of everything), so a cleared run_id box would otherwise dump the unfiltered stream of both services here. The run_id variable's default is the sentinel 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, which cannot occur in real logs, so a fresh load or a cleared box shows nothing instead of everything. Paste a real run id to see its lines.

targets.expr: {service=~"fastapi|browser-service|runner-exec"} |= "$run_id" | json | level=~"$level" | line_format "{{ if .event }}{{.level}} {{.logger}} :: {{.event}}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}"

options.content:
The generated `.robot` code and the Robot `log.html` report are files, not database rows, and are not rendered here.

Open [Mark 1 History](http://localhost:3000/history) and paste the run id into the search box — it searches run ids server-side — then use the drawer for the code and the report link.
